title: Payroll roster and terminations, January to June 2026

title: Hypervisor manager user list, BMC account settings and log settings

title: Cloud tenant identity and configuration export

title: Customer portal settings, user and MFA report, and update history

title: PSA vault permissions and feature settings

title: Team password vault audit report

title: Customer and service list
source_system: Portal billing module and customer records (SYS-01)
what_it_shows: About 70 business customers, mostly in Florida: professional services firms, small manufacturers, local retailers and e-commerce sites, and 2 community banks; about 260 customer VMs, about 145 of them on the backup add-on; 22 managed services customers with about 310 servers; about 190 DNS zones; no federal agency customer

title: Bank A and Bank B vendor contracts with security exhibits
what_it_shows: Bank A, a national bank: 6 hosted VMs (loan document imaging and a file server) and RMM patching of 8 branch servers. Bank B, a state-chartered nonmember bank: RMM patching and backup monitoring of 9 servers in its own office. Both contracts state that the services are subject to the Bank Service Company Act, require the company to implement appropriate measures designed to meet the objectives of the Interagency Guidelines Establishing Information Security Standards, and require notice to the bank within 24 hours of unauthorized access to the bank's customer information; neither asks the company to notify the bank's customers or regulator

title: Bank contact file

title: Master services agreement and managed services addendum
what_it_shows: 99.9% monthly availability for hosting, with service credits of 10% below 99.9% and 25% below 99.0%; security incident notice to affected customers without undue delay and within 72 hours of confirmation; confidentiality clause; customers back up their own VMs unless they buy the backup add-on and patch their own guest operating systems unless they buy managed services; PHI, CUI, covered defense information and payment card data are prohibited; acceptable use terms allow suspension of a VM; the managed services addendum has no script approval terms

title: AI triage tests and MDR service manager interview
source_system: MDR July 2026 alert export and automated-action log; escalation summaries; MDR service manager interview (2026-08-25)
what_it_shows: July 2026: about 2,140 alerts on company telemetry, about 91% auto-closed with no human review, 52 reviewed by MDR analysts, 7 escalated to the company. In a random sample of 100 auto-closed alerts, 2 had needed investigation. 2 of 20 escalation summaries named the wrong laptop and 1 described a blocked sign-in as successful. June to August 2026: 3 automatic laptop isolations and 2 automatic account suspensions; 81% of user-behavior alerts and both suspensions fell on technical staff working after hours or from DC-1, all false positives. The provider set the auto-close and containment settings at onboarding; the company never approved them

title: Control assessment: account management review and tests
source_system: User lists of the identity provider, VPN, RMM tool, hypervisor manager, cloud tenant, DNS account and PSA; staff roster; termination record; colocation authorized-person list (facility desk, 2026-08-18); Operations Manager and Lead Systems Engineer interviews
what_it_shows: 2 shared RMM support accounts and 1 shared hypervisor administrator account in daily use; every RMM technician account can act on all 22 managed customers; accounts are created on an email request with no recorded approval; no account procedure or account review record; the former Support Engineer's VPN account was enabled from 2026-03-13 to 2026-07-22; the colocation authorized-person list still named him at the DC-1 walkthrough on 2026-08-18, and he was removed that day; the shared RMM password and MFA seed were unchanged until 2026-07-23; Support Engineers hold no cluster or cloud administrator rights; account types were documented only in the draft POL-02 Part B

title: Control assessment: separation of duties test
source_system: RMM test script against the company's lab VMs; RMM and backup role settings; draft POL-02 B.5
what_it_shows: One engineer account created and scheduled a harmless test script against the company's own lab VMs with no approval step, and the tool would have let it target all 22 customers; the same account can delete backups; duties that need two people were listed only in the draft POL-02 B.5

title: Control assessment: privilege review
source_system: Role exports from the hypervisor manager, identity provider, cloud tenant, RMM tool and PSA vault
what_it_shows: The portal service account holds full administrator rights in the hypervisor manager; the Owner uses standing administrator accounts in the identity provider, cloud tenant and RMM tool; all 7 staff can read every PSA vault entry, including bank server passwords

title: Control assessment: remote access review and sign-in test
source_system: VPN, RMM and cloud sign-in settings; RMM sign-in from a mobile hotspot with an assessment-only account (deleted the same day); draft POL-02 B.8
what_it_shows: The VPN requires identity provider MFA; the RMM and cloud consoles have no source-address restriction, and the assessment-only RMM account signed in from a mobile hotspot; each remote access type in use was set up by the Lead Systems Engineer with the Owner's agreement; usage restrictions were written only in the draft POL-02 B.8

title: Control assessment: privileged MFA test
source_system: Hypervisor manager sign-in over the VPN; BMC, RMM and identity provider MFA settings
what_it_shows: Once on the VPN, the hypervisor manager accepted the shared administrator password alone; BMCs use passwords only; the shared RMM accounts' one-time codes come from a seed in the team vault; identity provider push approval has no number matching

title: Control assessment: authenticator review and default-password check
source_system: Default-password check of every DC-1 management interface (2026-08-18); vault audit report; 2 onboarding records from 2025; portal VM configuration; interviews
what_it_shows: The backup appliance accepted the vendor's default administrator password on 2026-08-18, and the password was changed on 2026-08-19; BMC passwords are 8 characters, shared across all 6 hosts and unchanged since 2022; the portal service account password is in plain text on the portal VM; no written procedure for lost or compromised authenticators; new staff receive accounts and enroll MFA in person on their first day; initial passwords are generated by the password manager and must be changed at first sign-in; all 7 staff use the password manager

title: Control assessment: backup review
source_system: Backup job report (July 2026); backup and bucket settings; cloud audit trail (90 days) and role export received 2026-08-17
what_it_shows: Nightly backups of the 145 add-on VMs completed on 30 of 31 nights in July 2026, and the failed night was re-run the next day; nightly hypervisor manager configuration backup and portal database dump; customer DNS zones and the PSA documentation have no copy outside their SaaS providers; the backup repository is not encrypted at rest; the cloud copy is not immutable, sits in the portal's account, and any cloud administrator can change or delete it; no two-person approval for deletion

title: Control assessment: contingency plan and test records
source_system: Document request; Lead Systems Engineer and Systems Engineer interviews
what_it_shows: No contingency plan and no test records were provided; customer restores, about 2 a month, are not recorded

title: Control assessment: monitoring coverage review and RMM alert test
source_system: MDR data source list and July 2026 monthly report (received 2026-08-12); July 2026 auto-close statistics and automated-action log (received 2026-08-14); RMM sign-in and test script (2026-08-18); Lead Systems Engineer interview
what_it_shows: MDR sources are the laptops, the identity provider and the firewalls; no hypervisor manager, BMC, RMM, cloud tenant or DNS source; the RMM sign-in from a non-company address and the test script raised no alert; MDR analysts and the AI triage analyze detected events 24x7, and about 91% of about 2,140 July 2026 alerts were auto-closed with no review at the company; the MDR escalates to the on-call engineer by phone and sends a monthly report; the monitoring notice to staff was written only in the draft POL-02 C.6

title: Control assessment: log review interviews
source_system: Lead Systems Engineer and Owner interviews
what_it_shows: Nobody reviews RMM, hypervisor manager, cloud tenant or DNS logs, or the alerts the AI triage closes; MDR findings reach only the Lead Systems Engineer and are not reported to the Owner; no rule to adjust review after threat information

title: Control assessment: incident reporting interviews
source_system: Interviews with 5 of 7 staff; bank contact file; draft POL-03
what_it_shows: No reporting time rule other than the draft POL-03 4.2; 3 of 5 staff interviewed did not know whom to call after hours; Bank A's designated contact left in 2024 and Bank B never gave one; the 24-hour contract notice and the 4-hour bank rule were in no procedure in effect

title: Control assessment: vendor agreement and assurance review
source_system: Contract folder; RMM and MDR terms; colocation SOC 2 report; vendor evidence requests sent 2026-08-10
what_it_shows: The RMM contract has no security requirements; the RMM and MDR providers have never been reviewed; the MDR contract allows use of de-identified telemetry to improve its models; the RMM and MDR SOC 2 reports requested on 2026-08-10 were not received by 2026-08-19; the colocation SOC 2 report was last read in 2024 before this engagement; the P04 responsibility mapping and the colocation complementary user entity controls define who does what for each provider; vendor oversight was written only in the draft POL-02 A.5

title: Control assessment: termination review
source_system: Termination record (2026-03-13); VPN, RMM and colocation records; Operations Manager interview
what_it_shows: The former Support Engineer's VPN access was disabled four months after he left; the shared RMM password and MFA seed he knew were unchanged until 2026-07-23; his colocation access was revoked on 2026-08-18; no exit interview or confidentiality reminder; laptop and colocation badge were returned and his mailbox and PSA tickets reassigned on the last day
